chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn al-Mughira, from Abu

Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: When the believer reaches forty years, Allah secures him from three illnesses: leprosy, albinism, and madness. So when he reaches fifty, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, lightens his accounting. When he reaches sixty years, Allah grants him repentance (return to God). So when he reaches seventy, the inhabitants of the sky love him. When he reaches eighty, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commands to record his good deeds and cast away his bad deeds. When he reaches ninety, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, forgives him what preceded of his sin and what followed, and writes him as a prisoner of Allah in His earth. And in another report: When he reaches a hundred, that is the feeblest (end) of life.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for a Muslim at ages 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, and 100 according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the concept of 'gradual spiritual maturation,' where aging is viewed not as decline but as a progressive elevation in divine favor and accountability. The progression from physical protection at forty to the ultimate status of 'Asir Allah' (Prisoner of God) at ninety highlights the accumulation of wisdom and the lightening of the scales, culminating in the view that reaching one hundred marks the end of the earthly trial. This narrative reinforces the Shia emphasis on patience and continuous repentance throughout the lifespan as a means to secure divine mercy.
